classification.difficultyReason: Three linked right-triangle steps: sine, tangent inverse, then add horizontal distances on opposite sides.

content.prompt:
A flagpole stands on level ground. Two ropes run from the top of the pole to pegs $A$ and $B$ on opposite sides of the pole.
The rope to peg $A$ is $14\text{ m}$ long and makes an angle of $55^\circ$ with the ground.
Peg $B$ is $9.5\text{ m}$ from the base of the pole.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
How high is the flagpole?
Answer correct to one decimal place.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What angle, to the nearest degree, does the rope to peg $B$ make with the ground?

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the distance between the pegs. Answer to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
The pegs are on opposite sides of the pole.
$$\begin{align*}AD&=14\cos55^\circ\\AB&=AD+DB\\AB&=14\cos55^\circ+9.5\\AB&\approx17.5\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
